sources.citation: Himes, Ronald S. 1997. Reconstructions in Kalinga-Itneg. Oceanic Linguistics 36(1):102-134. doi:10.2307/3623072.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Classifies Ibanaw of Daguioman, Malibcong, Talalang and Balbalasang as Northwestern Kalinga; sec. 2 phonology reconstructs segments and *V: (length) only; the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur; data are the author's own field notes (1962-1995).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Kalinga language' (Banao Itneg redirects there) and 'Itneg language'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Generic Kalinga inventory from Gieser 1958 (Guinaang); the only stress remark (chílu 'honey' vs chilú 'dew', 'otherwise stress is not usually marked') concerns the Lubuagan Kalinga orthography, not Banao.

sources.citation: OLAC. Resources in and about the Banao Itneg language (as of 2024-07-19).
sources.note: Lists only the five SIL wordlists above plus Glottolog/Ethnologue/LINGUIST List entries; no grammar or phonology item exists for bjx.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue 19th ed., entry 'Itneg, Banao' (the Internet Archive 2016).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Locations (Balbalan, Pasil; Daguioman, Malibcong), 3,500 speakers (2003 SIL), dialects Malibcong Banao, Banao Pikekj, Gubang Itneg, lexical-similarity figures; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Walton, Charles & Janice R. Walton. 2003. Banao, Malibcong, Abra wordlist (1966 Expanded Philippine Word List, 372 items, informant Conception Paredes Maliwanan, 6/2/03). SIL Philippines archive item 77404, tagged bjx (Malibcong Banao dialect).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Handwritten list with stress ticks per word ('tikling, 'kulap, 'soso, 'mammanok vs lo'san, gidgi'tsam, fo'nog, napa'?it); no notes, no rule.

sources.citation: Walton, Charles. 2003. Banao and Masadiit, Pikek, Dagioman, Abra wordlist (1966 Expanded Philippine Word List, 372 items). SIL Philippines archive item 77402, tagged bjx.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Handwritten phonetic list with a raised tick before the stressed syllable ('losan, 'kulap, 'utok, 'susu vs napa'?it, na'ngitit); no notes, no rule.

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 1974. The Central Cordilleran subgroup of Philippine languages. Oceanic Linguistics 13:511-560; Reid 1973, Diachronic typology of Philippine vowel systems; Reid (ed.) 1971, Philippine minor languages.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: 1974: PCC had 'fourteen consonants, four vowels and stress'; mentions -taku in 'Banaw Itneg' (Walton pers. comm.) only. 1973: 'Banaw subdialect of Tingguian.. Daguioman' cited for consonant allophones only. 1971: no Banao entry. Nothing on Banao stress placement.

sources.citation: Busenitz, Robert L. & C. Richard Gieser. 1973. Balbalasang Kalinga wordlist (1966 Expanded Philippine Word List, 372 items, informant Brent Banganan, Balbalasang, Balbalan; one page of phonological notes). SIL Philippines Language & Culture Archives item 77098, tagged Banao Itneg [bjx].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Notes page treats only /b/ /d/ /l/ allophones, glottal-stop orthography and /g/ devoicing; nothing on stress. The typed list marks stress by acute accent on individual words (abaká, ámin, súlag, tiklíng, sungbát, buwá, gabú, bálat, lawód, dakól, napaít, úlos, dála, útok, súsu, sobgón, kollápoy, úbot): both penult and final occur; no rule stated.

sources.citation: Roe, G. Richard & Lester O. Troyer. 1957. Kalinga-Itneg comparative wordlists (Yale Questionnaire list in Guinaang, Balbalasang, Gacab [Banao], Bangilo, Mataragan; 7 pp. + cover; two texts). SIL Philippines archive item 77407, tagged bjx, kkg, knb.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Cover 'Symbolization' covers k, f, c, l, u only; nothing on stress. Raw comparative data.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid bana1288 and reference 319229; Grambank, language bana1288 (coder Jingting Ye).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only descriptive reference is Ramos 1970; Grambank coded solely from it; no stress information.

sources.citation: Ramos, Patria Pilosas. 1970. The verbal sentences of Bhanaw Tinggian. MA thesis, University of the Philippines Diliman (adviser Ernesto Constantino). 53 pp. Call no. LG 995 1970 L5 /R35, UP Dept. of Linguistics code DLL-0376.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only description Glottolog lists for bjx; Constantino-school UP theses of this era usually open with a short phonology section that lists stress as a phoneme and may state its placement. A scan exists in Hammarström's collection (Glottolog bestfn) and was used by Grambank, so a copy can be requested from Glottolog/Grambank or from UP Diliman.

sources.citation: Walton, Charles. 1965. The phonemes of Binongan Itneg (Tinguian). Unpublished SIL Philippines paper (cited in Reid ed. 1971 as the source of the Binongan Itneg phonology).

sources.note: Closest published phonology of a Kalinga variety (Guinaang, Lubuagan Kalinga [knb]); Himes 1997 groups Balbalasang Banao with Kalinga and the 1973 Balbalasang notes say 'as in Guinaang'. Would give a Kalinga-level stress statement to compare, though not Banao itself.
